arxiv-2301-04331.title: Nucleon Electric Dipole Moment from the θ \theta Term with Lattice Chiral Fermions
arxiv-2301-04331.creator: Jian Liang, Andrei Alexandru, Terrence Draper, Keh-Fei Liu, Bigeng Wang, Gen Wang, Yi-Bo Yang
arxiv-2301-04331.description: Abstract We calculate the nucleon electric dipole moment (EDM) from the θ \theta term with overlap fermions on three domain wall lattices with different sea pion masses at lattice spacing 0.11 fm. Due to the chiral symmetry conserved by the overlap fermions, we have well defined topological charge and chiral limit for the EDM.

arxiv-2306-00578.title: Does Black-box Attribute Inference Attacks on Graph Neural Networks Constitute Privacy Risk?
arxiv-2306-00578.creator: Iyiola E. Olatunji, Anmar Hizber, Oliver Sihlovec, Megha Khosla
arxiv-2306-00578.description: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown promising results on real-life datasets and applications, including healthcare, finance, and education. However, recent studies have shown that GNNs are highly vulnerable to attacks such as membership inference attack and link reconstruction attack. Surprisingly, attribute inference attacks has received little attention.

arxiv-2307-02285.title: Monolithic atom interferometry
arxiv-2307-02285.creator: Johannes Fiedler, Kim Lefmann, Wolf von Klitzing, Bodil Holst
arxiv-2307-02285.description: Abstract Atom and, more recently, molecule interferometers are used in fundamental research and industrial applications. Most atom interferometers rely on gratings made from laser beams, which can provide high precision but cannot reach very short wavelengths and require complex laser systems to function.

arxiv-2308-11088.title: Collaborative Route Planning of UAVs, Workers and Cars for Crowdsensing in Disaster Response
arxiv-2308-11088.creator: Lei Han, Chunyu Tu, Zhiwen Yu, , Zhiyong Yu, , Weihua Shan, Liang Wang, and Bin Guo
arxiv-2308-11088.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lei Han, Chunyu Tu, Zhiwen Yu, , Zhiyong Yu, , Weihua Shan, Liang Wang, and Bin Guo. Efficiently obtaining the up-to-date information in the disaster-stricken area is the key to successful disaster response. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), workers and cars can collaborate to accomplish sensing tasks, such as data collection, in disaster-stricken areas. In this paper, we explicitly address the route planning for a group of agents, including UAVs, workers, and cars, with the goal of maximizing the task completion rate.

arxiv-2403-00033.title: Spatial Craving Patterns in Marijuana Users: Insights from fMRI Brain Connectivity Analysis with High-Order Graph Attention Neural Networks
arxiv-2403-00033.creator: Jun-En Ding, Shihao Yang, Anna Zilverstand, Kaustubh R. Kulkarni, Xiaosi Gu, Fegn Liu
arxiv-2403-00033.description: Abstract The excessive consumption of marijuana can induce substantial psychological and social consequences. In this investigation, we propose an elucidative framework termed high-order graph attention neural networks (HOGANN) for the classification of Marijuana addiction, coupled with an analysis of localized brain network communities exhibiting abnormal activities among chronic marijuana users.

arxiv-2403-03685.title: Correlations of fluctuations of two-dimensional flow forced by a random force on top of a shear flow
arxiv-2403-03685.creator: I.V.Kolokolov 1 2 {}^{1}\,{}^{2} , V.V.Lebedev 1 2 {}^{1}\,{}^{2}
arxiv-2403-03685.description: Abstract We examine fluctuations of vorticity excited by an external random force in two-dimensional fluid in the presence of a strong external shear flow. The problem is motivated by the analysis of big coherent vortices appearing as a consequence of the inverse energy cascade in a finite box at large Reynolds numbers.

arxiv-2410-16261.title: Mini-InternVL: A Flexible-Transfer Pocket Multimodal Model with 5% Parameters and 90% Performance
arxiv-2410-16261.creator: Zhangwei Gao Zhe Chen Erfei Cui Yiming Ren Weiyun Wang, Jinguo Zhu Hao Tian Shenglong Ye Junjun He Xizhou Zhu Lewei Lu, Tong Lu Yu Qiao Jifeng Dai Wenhai Wang
arxiv-2410-16261.description: Abstract Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance in vision-language tasks across a broad spectrum of domains. However, the large model scale and associated high computational costs pose significant challenges for training and deploying MLLMs on consumer-grade GPUs or edge devices, thereby hindering their widespread application.

arxiv-2502-18825.title: The distance of quasar outflows from the central source: The first consistent values from emission and absorption determinations.
arxiv-2502-18825.creator: Mayank Sharma, Nahum Arav, Qinyuan Zhao, Maryam Dehghanian, Doyee Byun, Gwen Walker, Luming Sun, Lu Shen, Yulong Gao, Guilin Liu, Junfeng Wang
arxiv-2502-18825.description: Abstract Measuring the distance of quasar outflows from the central source ( R R ) is essential for determining their importance for AGN feedback. There are two methods to measure R R : 1) A direct determination using spatially resolved Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS) of the outflow in emission.

arxiv-2503-18046.title: Non-(strong, geometrically) ergodicity criteria for discrete time Markov chains on general state spaces
arxiv-2503-18046.creator: Ling-Di Wang, Yu Chen, Yu-Hui Zhang
arxiv-2503-18046.description: Abstract For discrete-time Markov chains on general state spaces, we establish criteria for non-ergodicity and non-strong ergodicity, and derive sufficient conditions for non-geometric ergodicity via the theory of minimal nonnegative solutions. Our criteria are formulated based on the existence of solutions to inequalities involving the chain’s one-step transition kernel.

arxiv-2504-16735.title: An Expressive Coalgebraic Modal Logic for Cellular Automata
arxiv-2504-16735.creator: Henning Basold, Chase Ford, Lulof Pirée
arxiv-2504-16735.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Henning Basold, Chase Ford, Lulof Pirée. Cellular automata provide models of parallel computation based on cells, whose connectivity is given by an action of a monoid on the cells. At each step in the computation, every cell is decorated with a state that evolves in discrete steps according to a local update rule, which determines the next state of a cell based on its neighbour’s states.

arxiv-2510-11056.creator: Runze Xia, Yupeng Ji, Yuxi Zhou, Haodong Liu, Teng Zhang, Piji Li
arxiv-2510-11056.description: Abstract . Query-service relevance prediction in e-commerce search systems faces strict latency requirements that prevent the direct application of Large Language Models (LLMs). To bridge this gap, we propose a two-stage reasoning distillation framework to transfer reasoning capabilities from a powerful teacher LLM to a lightweight, deployment-friendly student model.

arxiv-2511-10788.title: From Efficiency to Adaptivity: A Deeper Look at Adaptive Reasoning in Large Language Models
arxiv-2511-10788.creator: Chao Wu, Baoheng Li, Mingchen Gao, Zhenyi Wang
arxiv-2511-10788.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chao Wu, Baoheng Li, Mingchen Gao, Zhenyi Wang. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have made reasoning a central benchmark for evaluating intelligence. While prior surveys focus on efficiency by examining how to shorten reasoning chains or reduce computation, this view overlooks a fundamental challenge: current LLMs apply uniform reasoning strategies regardless of task complexity, generating long traces for trivial problems while failing to extend reasoning for difficult tasks.

pmc-13283346.title: Severe Hyperammonemic Encephalopathy Associated With Gastrointestinal Bleeding During Capecitabine and Oxaliplatin Chemotherapy in a Patient With Rectal Adenocarcinoma
pmc-13283346.creator: Taiga Komatsu, Veevek Anand Agrawal
pmc-13283346.description: Hyperammonemic encephalopathy is a rare complication of fluoropyrimidine and platinum-based chemotherapy that can occur independently of hepatic dysfunction. While gastrointestinal bleeding is a well-established precipitant of hyperammonemia in cirrhosis, its role in patients treated with chemotherapy without liver disease has rarely been reported.

pmc-13381246.title: Protocol for a clinical practice guideline on acupuncture for chronic non-specific low back pain
pmc-13381246.creator: Jiacheng Zhang, Yusheng Li, Gaoxinli Liu, Shun Fan, Peizhen Zhang, Qiaoling Chen, Jing Ning, Huanan Li, Jingui Wang

Acupuncture can effectively relieves pain, improve function, and avoid adverse drug reactions.
